hints: Take logarithms of both positive sides so that the variable exponents become coefficients.
Expand to \(\ln2+(1-2x)\ln3<x\ln5\) and collect all x-terms on one side.
When dividing by the resulting logarithmic coefficient, check its sign before stating the exact inequality.
walkthrough:
Since both sides of the inequality are strictly positive for all real $x$, take natural logarithms of both sides without reversing the inequality sign:
$$\ln\left(2 \times 3^{1-2x}\right) < \ln\left(5^x\right)$$

Apply the product rule of logarithms $\ln(ab) = \ln a + \ln b$ to the left-hand side:
$$\ln 2 + \ln\left(3^{1-2x}\right) < \ln\left(5^x\right)$$

Apply the power rule of logarithms $\ln(u^k) = k\ln u$ to both logarithmic terms with exponents:
$$\ln 2 + (1 - 2x)\ln 3 < x\ln 5$$

Expand the brackets on the left-hand side:
$$\ln 2 + \ln 3 - 2x\ln 3 < x\ln 5$$

Combine the constant terms using the product rule $\ln 2 + \ln 3 = \ln(2 \times 3) = \ln 6$:
$$\ln 6 - 2x\ln 3 < x\ln 5$$

Collect all terms containing $x$ on the right-hand side:
$$\ln 6 < x\ln 5 + 2x\ln 3$$

Factorise $x$ out of the terms on the right-hand side:
$$\ln 6 < x(\ln 5 + 2\ln 3)$$

Simplify the coefficient of $x$ using the power rule and product rule of logarithms:
$$2\ln 3 = \ln\left(3^2\right) = \ln 9$$
$$\ln 5 + 2\ln 3 = \ln 5 + \ln 9 = \ln(5 \times 9) = \ln 45$$

Rewrite the inequality with the simplified logarithm:
$$\ln 6 < x\ln 45$$

Since $45 > 1$, $\ln 45 > 0$. Divide both sides by $\ln 45$ without reversing the inequality sign:
$$x > \dfrac{\ln 6}{\ln 45}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equa: Applies the law of the logarithm of a product or power. Derives \(x>\frac{\ln6}{\ln45}\). The final result is \(\displaystyle x>\frac{\ln6}{\ln45}\).
